summary.oneLiner: One of India's leading integrated manufacturers of solar and conventional pumping solutions, renewable energy products and EV motors/controllers, with an estimated ~25% market share under the PM-KUSUM scheme and a presence across 100+ countries.
summary.business: Shakti Pumps (India) Limited manufactures and sells submersible pumps, motors, VFDs, inverters and their spare parts, with core products spanning solar pump sets, agricultural pumps and industrial pumps. Its portfolio extends to smart monitoring solutions, rooftop solar products and EV components (motors, controllers and chargers), delivered to agriculture, water management, industrial and clean-energy applications. The Company operates a backward-integrated manufacturing model and sells through Government Projects, Industrial, OEM, Retail and Export channels.

currentContext.expansion: Shakti Pumps has committed `17,000 Mn to a capacity expansion programme, described in the FY26 Key Milestones as covering an advanced 2.2 GW solar manufacturing platform, a doubling of capacity for pumps, motors, VFDs and solar structures, and the establishment of a manufacturing facility for EV motors, controllers and chargers under Shakti EV Mobility Pvt. Ltd. The Corporate Overview frames this as phased capacity build-out - 'continuous investments in R&D, integrated manufacturing, automation and phased capacity including 2.2 GW Solar DCR Cell and PV Module manufacturing' - positioned as a long-term competitive advantage through backward integration. The existing footprint is four integrated manufacturing facilities headquartered at Pithampur, Madhya Pradesh, with backward-integrated capability across pumps, motors, controllers, inverters, VFDs, solar structures and allied components; earlier milestones record establishment of an SEZ unit and expansion of the core facility to 5,00,000 pump capacity. Wholly owned subsidiary Shakti Energy Solutions Ltd., located in Pithampur (MP), currently does only captive production and has plans to sell to other players as well. The routed sections give no commissioning, ramp-up or completion dates for the announced expansion, and no project-wise capex split.

risks.risk: Energy cost and grid availability in manufacturing
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk: electricity constitutes a significant operating expense in the manufacture of water pumps, and escalating power tariffs, interruptions in grid availability and reliance on conventional energy sources may lead to higher production costs and disrupt manufacturing schedules. Mitigation is through energy-consumption tracking, energy-efficient technologies, renewable energy integration and peak demand management.

risks.risk: Raw material and component sourcing concentration
risks.note: BRSR flags that pumps require certain metals and components that may have limited global suppliers and be subject to price volatility or geopolitical risk; disruptions can delay production and impact margins. Mitigated by supplier diversification, long-term supply agreements, alternative materials and strategic inventory reserves.

risks.risk: Workforce health and safety in heavy manufacturing
risks.note: Employees are exposed to occupational risks from heavy equipment, electrical systems and movement of large or cumbersome materials; shortcomings in safety practices may lead to injuries, production disruption, regulatory consequences and reputational damage. Managed through stringent SOPs, periodic training, mandatory PPE, preventive maintenance and hazard/incident reporting.

risks.risk: Talent attrition in a competitive renewable energy labour market
risks.note: Permanent-employee turnover rose to 26.03% in FY2025-26 from 10.24% in FY2024-25. The Company attributes this to early attrition among freshers who were unwilling to work in the assigned domain despite it being communicated at campus hiring, and to newly established regional renewable-segment companies offering higher compensation and benefits.

The BRSR reports 100% of turnover from a single main activity - manufacture of electrical equipment and general/special purpose machinery - and 100% of turnover from the manufacture of pumps, leaving the business without a diversifying revenue line outside the pumping and allied equipment franchise.

risks.risk: Dependence on government schemes and institutional buyers
risks.note: Government institutions are described as a significant customer group, with the Company playing a vital role in flagship rural solarisation initiatives such as PM-KUSUM. Scheme design, tendering pace and policy change therefore drive a material share of demand.

Export sales represented approximately 13.75% of total turnover during the reporting period, spread across more than 100 countries and served through international agencies, project developers and institutional buyers, exposing the business to overseas demand, currency and geopolitical conditions.

risks.risk: External macro, policy, technology and climate factors flagged in the forward-looking statement
risks.note: Management explicitly cautions that actual results may differ materially due to changes in economic conditions, government policies, regulatory developments, industry dynamics, technological advancements, competitive intensity, geopolitical events and climate-related risks.

one-line thesis: Shakti Pumps delivered record revenue (INR 858cr Q4) but saw margins compress to ~10% due to raw material inflation and low-realization state tenders; the critical pivot is a massive INR 420cr receivables reduction improving cash flows, setting the stage for margin recovery via backward integration (solar cell plant) and KUSUM 2.0 demand.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 858cr (Q4), INR 2,698cr (FY26) - Record highs; EBITDA Margin: ~10% (Q4), ~16% (FY26) - Pressured by RM costs & Magel Tyala scheme; PAT: Impacted by 42% effective tax rate in Q4 (one-off provisions); Order Book: INR 1,500cr (as of May 7, 2026); Net Debt: Improved cash conversion with INR 124cr operating cash flow in FY26; One-offs: High Q4 tax due to warranty/CSR/dividend tax provisions.
guidance: Revenue: No specific number, targeting YoY growth; Margin: Expect improvement in H2FY27 as RM costs normalize and solar plant commissions; Order Inflow: KUSUM 2.0 orders expected Q2FY27; Capex: Solar module (0.5GW) by Q1FY27 end, Solar cell (2.2GW) by Mar'28.
order book & pipeline: INR 1,500 crores (ex-GST clarification requested by analysts), sufficient for next 2 quarters; ~INR 500cr from Maharashtra (lower margin), rest diversified across states.
segment / subsidiary detail: Solar Pumps: 86,086 units installed in FY26 (+20% YoY), 28,345 in Q4 (+51% YoY); Rooftop: Early stage, focusing on inverter efficiency (claimed 10% better generation); EV: Pre-revenue, vehicle-level trials ongoing, revenue expected in 6-12 months.
growth verticals / optionality: KUSUM 2.0 national rollout replacing diesel pumps; Export recovery post-geopolitical stabilization; Rooftop solar scaling via channel partners; EV motor commercialization.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 margins hit by 6-7% raw material inflation (copper, steel, silicon), 3-4% lower realization from Magel Tyala scheme, and 2-3% operating leverage benefit; Export margins ~10% higher than domestic.
capex / expansion: FY26: INR 70cr invested in EV line (of INR 114cr planned); FY27: Commissioning 0.5GW module plant (Q1FY27) and 2.2GW cell plant (Mar'28).
capital allocation: Priority on working capital normalization (receivables reduced by INR 420cr in Q4); Funding growth via internal accruals to avoid undue leverage.
risks & watch-items: Delay in KUSUM 2.0 announcement; Sustained high raw material prices; Payment delays from state discoms despite recent improvements; Competitive intensity in L1 tenders.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; Emphasizes balance sheet discipline over aggressive growth; Confident in long-term demand but acknowledges temporary margin headwinds.
non-obvious takeaways: Receivables of INR 1,276cr include INR 916cr 'not due' pending RMS data validation (7-90 days post-install), implying imminent cash inflow rather than bad debt; Management explicitly rejected nuclear/hydrogen diversification to stay focused on solar core.

themes.title: Renewable IPP / FDRE firm-power & storage
themes.need: DISCOMs mandating firm/round-the-clock RE make BESS + pumped-hydro the bid differentiator, and in Q1FY27 storage demand ran ahead of supply. ADANIGREEN has 3.5 GWh of BESS installed (+1.9 GWh at Khavda this quarter), targets 10+ GWh this fiscal and 50 GWh by FY30 on a thumb-rule INR 25-30 lakh of EBITDA per MWh against ~INR 1.5cr/MWh of capex, and has contracted essentially all merchant/C&I capacity to sibling AESL on 25-year (solar/wind) and 15-year (battery) fixed-price PPAs targeting ~15-16% IRR - a pivot from merchant builder to fixed-return contracted IPP, with evacuation (not panels) named as the binding constraint. JSWENERGY added 873 MW in Q1 and ~1.1 GW since April - 36% of its 3 GW FY27 target already banked, Tidong Hydro commissioned four months early - and raised INR 10,150cr, taking net leverage 5.2x to 4.95x. On the equipment side SERVOTECH said its BESS pack capacity is fully booked ('we are not able to meet the demand') and committed to 2x capacity in 6 months, 3x by 21-Mar-2027 and 10x within 2 years. ACMESOLAR/KPIGREEN/SUZLON/INOXWIND attach storage to solar/wind; NTPC/NHPC/SJVN/TATAPOWER drive pumped-hydro and utility-scale storage.
themes.driver: BESS capacity commissioning against demand two independent managements (ADANIGREEN, SERVOTECH) say already exceeds supply; FDRE/peak-power tender awards; merchant DAM prices (JSWENERGY: INR 4.40 -> INR 5.10/unit, +16%) on +8.5% Q1 power demand.
